about.title: Loyalton Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Loyalton is a small Sierra County town, and its car accidents don't make headlines the way they might in a bigger city — but that doesn't make the aftermath any less disruptive for the person hurt. Public crash records show reported collisions here tend to cluster on Tuesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., often along Rt 49, Beckwith Road, Church Street, and around Courthouse Square, where local and through-traffic mix. Whether you were rear-ended on the highway or sideswiped downtown, the days right after a crash matter: insurers move fast, evidence disappears, and memories fade. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Loyalton with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened, explain your options, and handle communication with insurance companies. We're not a law firm and don't guarantee any result — but we can help you get a knowledgeable set of eyes on your situation quickly.

items.title: California's Filing Clock Moves Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government entity or road authority is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your Loyalton crash before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces your award rather than eliminating it. This matters on shared roads like Church Street or Courthouse Square where fault can be disputed.

items.title: Don't Hand the Insurer a Recorded Statement
items.desc: Adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can speak for you and help preserve evidence from the scene before it's lost.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Loyalton?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government vehicle or a road defect on a county- or state-maintained route, that deadline could be as short as six months. It's worth confirming your specific timeline with an attorney early.

items.question: There weren't many injury crashes reported in Loyalton recently — does that mean my case isn't serious?
items.answer: No. Public crash counts reflect town-wide totals, not the severity of what happened to you personally. Even in a small town like Loyalton, a single crash on Rt 49 or Beckwith Road can cause real, lasting injury, and your claim is evaluated on its own facts.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company before getting help?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other insurer before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters may use your words to reduce what they eventually offer. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can communicate with the insurer on your behalf.
